ukmt-grey-2017-01.title: Count between
ukmt-grey-2017-01.body:
Going left from Jess to Florence there are 3 girls between them; going right there are 6 between. Together with Jess and Florence: $3+6+2=11$.

**Answer: (C) 11**

ukmt-grey-2017-03.title: Compare sides
ukmt-grey-2017-03.body:
The outer rectangle is $3+4=7$ m longer and $2+3=5$ m taller than the inner one. Its perimeter exceeds the inner one by $2\times7+2\times5=24$ m.

**Answer: (E) 24 m**

ukmt-grey-2017-06.title: Convert minutes
ukmt-grey-2017-06.body:
$2017=33\times60+37$, so 2017 minutes is 33 h 37 min = 1 day 9 h 37 min. 9 h 37 min after 20:17 is 05:54 (the next day).

**Answer: (A) 05:54**

ukmt-grey-2017-08.title: Position from the left
ukmt-grey-2017-08.body:
Adam is at $\tfrac23$ of the pole from the left. Benny crawled $\tfrac34$ from the right end, so he is at $1-\tfrac34=\tfrac14$ from the left. They are $\tfrac23-\tfrac14=\tfrac{8-3}{12}=\tfrac5{12}$ of the pole apart.

**Answer: (E) $\tfrac5{12}$**

ukmt-grey-2017-09.title: Use the sums divisible by 5
ukmt-grey-2017-09.body:
Pair sums of $3,8,12,14$: only $3+12=15$ and $8+12=20$ are multiples of 5. Dan appears in both required sums, so Dan is 12, and Alan, Carl are 3 and 8. Alan is younger, so Alan is 3 and Carl is 8, leaving Bob as 14. Alan + Bob $=3+14=17$.

**Answer: (C) 17**

ukmt-grey-2017-12.title: Find the middle box
ukmt-grey-2017-12.body:
Add the first-three and last-three sums: $22+25=47$, which counts the middle box twice, so middle $=47-35=12$. The second box is $22-3-12=7$ and the fourth is $25-12-4=9$. Product $7\times9=63$.

**Answer: (D) 63**

ukmt-grey-2017-15.title: Count pairs of days
ukmt-grey-2017-15.body:
Pick the first day (7 ways); the second can be any day except itself and its two neighbours (4 ways). That gives 28 ordered pairs, so 14 unordered timetables.

**Answer: (C) 14**

ukmt-grey-2017-21.title: Find the period
ukmt-grey-2017-21.body:
The sequence is 2, 3, 6, 8, 8, 4, 2, 8, 6, 8, 8, 4, 2, 8, 6, ... After the first two terms the block 6, 8, 8, 4, 2, 8 repeats. $2017-2=2015=335\times6+5$, so the 2017th term is the 5th of the block: 2.

**Answer: (E) 2**

ukmt-grey-2017-24.title: Four corners
ukmt-grey-2017-24.body:
Each of the four $2\times2$ corner blocks must contain an uncoloured cell (otherwise the corner cell would have no uncoloured neighbour). So at least 4 cells are uncoloured and at most 12 coloured. An arrangement with 12 coloured cells exists, e.g. leave $(1,2),(2,4),(3,1),(4,3)$ uncoloured.

**Answer: (A) 12**
